_readme: GAME CONTENT: how PvE encounters are put together from enemy-library.json. Shapes are generated encounters: the runtime EncounterGenerator picks a variant (by Weight), draws each slot's count in [Min, Max] and each unit's type uniformly from Types, and keeps the draw only if its summed enemy Threat is inside [ThreatMin, ThreatMax], it has at least MinDistinctTypes types and it seats on the arena; units are placed front to back (Vanguard, Skirmisher, Ranged; library order within a stance). Each lineup then draws an element scheme by SchemeWeights (Uniform: one element for the whole team; PerType: one per type; PerUnit: one per unit; None), with elements dealt from a shuffled deck of the ten so every element is dealt before any repeats. Shape ids are drop-tables.json's shape ids (the validator requires the two sets to match): a cleared encounter pays out from its shape's drop cell. POST-GAME shapes (PostGame: true; the six *_postgame and *_postgame_hard shapes, drawn only by the post-game region r11, regions.json IsPostGame) are the exception: each pays out as the mainline shape its DropShapeId names (the same loot as that shape, on Normal and Hard alike), is calibrated by the balance simulator at level 100 only (TargetClear: squad and horde 65, elite 45 on Normal; 50, 50 and 30 on Hard), and stays out of the mainline report; its cells are appended to encounter-difficulty.json after the mainline ones. Any mainline rebalance must re-run --write-difficulty so they follow. Templates are authored fixed encounters ({ EncounterId, DisplayName, Description, ShapeId, Arena, Groups: [{ EnemyId, Count, Elements }], DifficultyOverride, Draft }; Elements are cycled over the group, empty = no element; DifficultyOverride 0 = use the shape's calibrated difficulty; Draft true = placeholder text/design pending producer review, never shown to the player). Hearthglen's fixed fights (hg_*, regions.json TutorialRegions FixedNodes; docs/design/area-zero.md) are templates too, each with its own DifficultyOverride tuned by the balance simulator's --mode hearthglen (docs/balance/hearthglen-report.md). The region bosses (regions.json's BossTemplateId, and the post-game region's HardMode.BossTemplateId) are the only templates, DRAFT placeholders pending producer review; each mainline DifficultyOverride is calibrated so the typical team from the owned roster (Tooling/BalanceSim --mode typical) at the boss's level wearing typical gear clears about 75%, the post-game twins (boss_r11_dusk_and_dawn, boss_r11_dusk_and_dawn_hard) about 35% on Normal and about 20% on Hard (docs/balance/tuning-log.md). Difficulty: every enemy's HP, Attack, Defense, SpecialAttack and SpecialDefense are multiplied by the shape's calibrated multiplier at the encounter's level (encounter-difficulty.json, written by the balance simulator's --write-difficulty, interpolated between the calibrated levels) times DifficultyScale. PENDING PRODUCER REVIEW: DifficultyScale is 1.0 and the table is calibrated so the typical team from the owned roster (Tooling/BalanceSim --mode typical; a sensible, not optimal pick, a producer decision) wearing typical gear (the balance simulator's --gear typical, a user decision) clears each shape's TargetClear (the tiered targets, a user decision: squad and horde 85%, elite and solo 75% (the producer's never-blocked targets: docs/balance/tuning-log.md, "Never-blocked targets"); encounter-difficulty.json records the target of every cell); whether the campaign should be that hard, and how a map node picks a shape and a level, are producer decisions not made here. Validated by EncounterLibraryValidator (the Editor importer Beast Craft/Data/Import Encounters, the EditMode tests, Tooling/BalanceSim): every shape's worst case (each slot at Max, each unit its slot's largest type) and every template must fit its arena's enemy deployment zone. The shapes and weights came over unchanged from the balance simulator's former fixtures; see docs/design/battle-system.md, 'Encounter direction'. Boss names and descriptions follow docs/design/content-bible.md; each boss carries Draft: true until the producer signs it off (the validator rejects a [DRAFT] marker in DisplayName/Description, which are player-facing); the calibration note that used to sit in each Description is this readme's (each mainline DifficultyOverride clears about 75% for the typical team at the boss's level in typical gear; the post-game twins about 35% on Normal and 20% on Hard).

Shapes.Description: One giant: huge HP, heavy single-target hits in both categories every turn and a periodic area slam in both. Compositions differ only in the giant's element.
A boss with an escort: one giant and two standard enemies, or two champions (mini-bosses) and one or two standard enemies.
Four to six standard enemies of at least three types: melee tanks, hunters, archers, casters and shamans.

Sixteen to twenty-four enemies: mostly swarm (tiny melee: swarmlings bite, physical; stinglings sting, special; one skill each, since every hit deals at least the damage floor), with a few archers and casters behind them.
Post-game (Duskmeridian, level 100): the squad recipe, calibrated harder. Pays out as a squad.
Post-game (Duskmeridian, level 100): the horde recipe, calibrated harder. Pays out as a horde.
Post-game (Duskmeridian, level 100): the elite recipe (dens and passes), calibrated harder. Pays out as an elite.
Post-game (Duskmeridian, level 100): the squad recipe, calibrated harder still, for Hard. Pays out as a squad.
Post-game (Duskmeridian, level 100): the horde recipe, calibrated harder still, for Hard. Pays out as a horde.
Post-game (Duskmeridian, level 100): the elite recipe (dens and passes), calibrated harder still, for Hard. Pays out as an elite.

Templates.Description: Two gloam-dazed scamps tumbling through the clover, snapping at anything that moves. They are more lost than fierce.
A buzzing knot of stinglings and a scamp that have made the old hedgerow their own. One of them hums with the green of the meadow.
An archer has taken the tumbled stones as a lookout, with a stingling darting between the rocks below.
A horned brute stands at the kinship stone, stamping in the brambles. Stand your ground beside your beast and another may choose to join you.
Scamps splash in the mill race while a caster mutters over the water. The mill wheel has stopped turning to listen.
A brute shakes the apple trees while an archer and a stingling help themselves to the windfalls. A draught of courage would not go amiss.
An old shaman keeps the second kinship stone, two scamps at its heels. Show it a team that stands together and a third beast will answer.
A stalker slinks along the ridge path with an archer and a pair of scamps. Your whole team, at last, can meet them together.

At the far hedge the shimmer thickens, and something big comes out of it: a champion of the vale, gloamed and bewildered, with two stinglings in its wake. Calm it, and the way to Verdant Hollow is open.
A mossy champion keeps the kinship stone, a horned brute and a lean stalker at its side. Stand firm and a beast of the Hollow may choose you.
A smouldering champion stands guard at the glowing stone with an archer and a caster behind it. Win and a beast of the ridges may answer.
A brine-soaked champion rises from the pool by the stone, a shaman and a brute wading after it. Win and a beast of the tides may choose you.
A gale-wrapped champion swoops down on the still stone with two stalkers circling. Win and a beast of the crags may answer.
A rust-plated champion guards the rooted stone, a brute and an archer beside it. Win and a beast of the iron wood may choose you.
A frost-bright champion keeps the glassy stone with a caster and a stalker. Win and a beast of the frozen lake may answer.
A dusk-cloaked champion rises from the shadow of the dark stone, a shaman and an archer behind it. Win and the last beast may choose you.
A moss-backed champion that once guarded the Hollow's Seal for the first Beastbinders and now guards it from everyone. Two horned brutes stamp at its side.
Twin fire champions who fight back to back on the ridge, trading sparks and grudges, while two archers pepper the field from the rocks above.
A barnacled water giant risen from the drowned ruins, with two casters chanting tide and frost from the shallows at its feet.
An air giant who walks the cloud line wrapped in its own gale, while three stalkers slip through the wind to pounce on stragglers.
Two great antlered champions, one of iron and one of stone, lock horns with anyone who nears the Seal. A shaman and two brutes keep the herd.
A towering ice giant who shelters a skittering brood of ten swarmlings under her skirts of snow, while two archers watch from the drifts.
The lightning giant holds court on the highest spire, a gale champion at its right hand and two casters crackling at its back.
The oldest living thing in the Deepwild: a nature giant grown half into the forest, wrapped in a humming cloud of twelve stinglings and tended by two shamans.
A fire giant crowned in cooling lava who sits the volcano's throne, flanked by two champions of stone and iron.
Two ancient giants, one of fire and one of water, who have guarded the Worldcrown's summit together since the first Seal was set. Where they meet, the Gloam rises.
Two ancient giants, one of radiant dawn and one of deepest dusk, who keep the endless evening beyond the Worldcrown in balance. They test every bond that comes this far.
The twin giants of Duskmeridian with halo and shadow at full blaze: the same pair, fiercer than any creature in the Farwild. Only the boldest Beastbinders ask for this.
